name: LeadFlow Demo — GHL Opportunity to Sheets

nodes.name: Log Unauthorized
nodes.notes: Deliberately logs NO caller-supplied value -- not the eventId, not the ids. An unauthenticated caller must not be able to write attacker-chosen content into the audit log.

nodes.name: Log Invalid Payload
nodes.notes: Logs the NAMES of the missing fields, taken from our own allowlist -- never the caller's values.

nodes.name: Respond 422
nodes.notes: 422 is deterministic and non-retryable: the same payload will always fail the same way, so a retry is pure noise.

nodes.name: Ledger: Look Up Event
nodes.notes: Always Output Data is ON deliberately: a miss must still emit an item, otherwise the whole new-event branch silently stops.

nodes.name: Log Duplicate Event
nodes.notes: Exactly one row. The correlationId differs from the first delivery's while the eventId matches -- that pairing is the evidence TC-02 is judged on.

nodes.name: Respond 200 already_processed
nodes.notes: 200, not 4xx. A duplicate is our plumbing's artifact, not the sender's error -- a 4xx here makes senders retry harder or page someone.

nodes.name: Ledger: Claim
nodes.notes: Claim BEFORE the backup write. Writing the ledger only afterwards means a crash in between produces a duplicate; writing it only before means a failure permanently suppresses the retry. This ordering is forced -- see ADR-002.

nodes.name: Sheets: leads_backup
nodes.notes: Append OR UPDATE, matched on eventId. If a previous delivery wrote this row and then died before the ledger reached 'completed', the retry updates that same row instead of adding a second one. This does not make the pipeline exactly-once -- it bounds the one failure mode the ledger's own ordering cannot.

nodes.name: Ledger: Record Attempt Outcome
nodes.notes: Left as 'failed', not deleted. A lost lead is unrecoverable; a duplicate is not. The row is what a reconciliation sweep would key on.

nodes.name: Log Attempt Outcome
nodes.notes: Best effort. If Google Sheets is the thing that broke, this write fails too -- which is why the ledger row, not this log, is the durable failure record.

nodes.name: Respond 500
nodes.notes: 500 invites a redelivery, and that is intended: the retry finds a 'claimed' or 'failed' ledger row, re-enters the branch, and the eventId-keyed backup write converges on one row.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'retry_scheduled', eventId: $('Retry Decision').first().json.eventId, attempt: $('Retry Decision').first().json.backupAttempt, maxAttempts: $('Retry Decision').first().json.maxAttempts, nextAttemptAt: $('Retry Decision').first().json.nextAttemptAt }) }}

value.reason: =leads_backup write failed on all {{ $('Retry Decision').first().json.maxAttempts }} attempts: {{ $('Retry Decision').first().json.lastError }}
